Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1042
Claimant:
James Hogan
Adjuster:
Valerie Rodriguez
5-8-24
Claim received for a side impact at an intersection, with the claimant reporting a neck strain and retaining cuonsel
before any statement was taken.
5-26-24
Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the intersection at the time of impact and confirms
the claimant was a passenger in that vehicle.
5-29-24
Driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force on the date of loss; nothing in the file suggests the damage
predates coverage.
6-12-24
Obtained photos from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses, all of which confirm the collision
happened as the claimant and the other driver described.
6-18-24
Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The driver-side door and quarter panel show clear impact damage consistent with a
side impact, though a few older scratches elsewhere on the body may predate this loss.
7-3-24
Medical records received show a neck strain diagnosis, and the mechanism and force of the collision appear
consistent with that type of injury.
8-29-24
No prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the records we obtained, and the claimant denies any earlier
complaints to that area.
9-9-24
Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication, with visit frequency tapering as the claimant
reported steady improvement.
9-27-24
Counsel forwarded a demand package. Reviewing whether all of the claimed vehicle damage and treatment can be
attributed to this impact, as the scope of some repairs is not yet clear.
11-2-24
Claimant provided a follow-up recorded statement adding a few small details about the moments before and after
impact; the core account remains the same as the initial report.
11-17-24
Compared the updated statement against the police report, witness accounts and photos, and found the sequence of
events consistent across all sources.
11-24-24
Reserve reviewed and file referred for final evaluation of the injury and property components, with the open question
on damage scope noted for the handling adjuster.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
